title: Project configuration digest codec
description: Objective: turn the browser-safe contract from task-0c21ba2f07cc4f4a829e475bbd7f0562 into the one canonical, content-addressed Node/domain manifest that daemon selection can trust. Deliverable: @moe/core public create/encode/decode functions that compose only the bare @moe/contracts root, domain-separate SHA-256 over canonical bytes of every ProjectConfigurationSettings field (settingsDigest is mechanically excluded from its own preimage), emit canonical full-manifest bytes, and fail closed on hostile/noncanonical/digest-mismatched input. NOT in scope: changing the contract vocabulary, daemon persistence/currentness, benchmark records, provider launch verification, or physical paths. Dependency: task-0c21ba2f07cc4f4a829e475bbd7f0562 must be DONE unchanged. Consumer: task-5dfc98fc3e7f4035a8012bd9ba032de3. Owned paths: packages/core/src/configuration/project-configuration-manifest.ts, its exact LF .js bridge, focused test, packages/core/src/index.ts, and packages/core/src/index-surface.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test && pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The @moe/core root exports typed immutable createProjectConfigurationManifest, encodeProjectConfigurationManifest, and decodeProjectConfigurationManifestBytes results plus a closed codec code/layer vocabulary; production imports task-0c21ba2f07cc4f4a829e475bbd7f0562 only through bare @moe/contracts.

SHA-256 is domain-separated over canonical bytes of every settings field except settingsDigest itself; object insertion order is irrelevant, fixed collections remain ordered, and the full encoded manifest including settingsDigest has one exact canonical byte representation.

Decode composes decodeBoundedJsonBytes, preserves duplicate-key provenance, snapshots once, revalidates the contract, recomputes the digest, and pins PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_BYTES_INVALID, PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DUPLICATE_KEY, PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_NONCANONICAL, or PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST_MISMATCH at the exact codec/canonicalization/digest layer; no malformed input throws.

A hand-enumerated production-surface sensitivity sweep asserts its exact positive leaf count and proves each valid leaf mutation changes settingsDigest while invalid mutations refuse; hostile byte/object cases pin exact code/layer/upstream, and valid results/bytes are frozen or caller-detached.

A reversible mutation removes one real production field from the canonical preimage and makes the named sensitivity test red before restoration; root namespace/type assertions and the exact LF bridge pass, and existing >250-line index.ts does not grow in physical line count.
The exact verification command exits 0, the manifest/lock/bare-specifier dependency probe is recorded, and task-5dfc98fc3e7f4035a8012bd9ba032de3 is recorded as the production consumer.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for creation, canonical bytes and the digest, in a new packages/core/src/configuration/project-configuration-manifest.test.ts. CANONICAL BYTES: encoding the same manifest twice yields byte-identical output; two settings objects built with their keys inserted in DIFFERENT orders produce the identical digest and identical bytes; and the `limits` table — a fixed ORDERED collection — keeps its declared order, so reordering two limit entries MUST change the digest. Assert both halves; a canonicalizer that sorts everything would silently make the limit order meaningless, and a canonicalizer that sorts nothing would make object key order significant. DOMAIN SEPARATION: the preimage carries a fixed domain tag, and a test proves that the same canonical JSON body hashed under a different tag yields a different digest — otherwise 'domain-separated' is a claim in a comment rather than a property. SETTINGSDIGEST EXCLUSION: changing ONLY manifest.settingsDigest leaves the RECOMPUTED digest unchanged (it is computed over settings, which structurally has no such field) while making decode refuse DIGEST_MISMATCH; assert both, because the first alone would also pass for a codec that ignores the field entirely. IMMUTABILITY: create/encode/decode results and their nested records are frozen, and no result object is identity-shared with the caller's input at any depth; mutating the caller's input after the call changes nothing in the result. Run and record the RED.
implementationPlan.note:
Wrote the creation / canonical-bytes / digest half of the focused test. RED recorded:
`pnpm vitest run --root . packages/core/src/configuration` -> EXIT=1, "Cannot find module './project-configuration-manifest.js'", 1 failed suite / 0 tests. Fails because the production module is absent, not because of a typo.

DESIGN CORRECTION MADE WHILE WRITING THE TESTS, recorded because it changes two drills.
The plan's step-2 wording assumed "reordering two limit entries MUST change the digest" is assertable. It is not: parseLimits enforces a DENSE POSITIONAL table (length must equal the vocabulary and entry i must already carry key i), so a reordered table is REFUSED upstream and never reaches the canonicalizer. Asserting a digest difference there was unreachable.
Replaced with an assertion that is bound to production bytes and does kill the mutant: the emitted `"key":"..."` sequence inside the encoded manifest must equal PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_LIMIT_KEYS in declared order. The vocabulary is NOT alphabetical, so a canonicalizer that sorted arrays would emit alphabetical order and redden. The test opens with an explicit CONTROL — `expect(declared).not.toEqual([...declared].sort())` — so the day the vocabulary becomes alphabetical the test fails instead of silently going vacuous.

EQUIVALENT-MUTANT DISCLOSURE, up front rather than discovered at drill time. Sorting OBJECT keys is not killable through this public surface and I will not claim it is. Every record the contract parser returns is rebuilt by a fixed object literal whose keys are already alphabetical at all eight levels (manifest, settings, policy, selection, network, isolation, schemaVersions, source, limit entry). create/encode/decode all validate through those parsers first, so the canonicalizer only ever sees an already-alphabetical record and removing the sort changes no byte. The sort stays as a defensive invariant and the production comment will say exactly this. What IS asserted is the end-to-end PROPERTY DoD 2 names — the same settings with every key inserted in reverse order yields the identical digest and identical bytes — which holds jointly through the parser's fixed construction and the sort.

Tests written (14): schema version + hex64 digest shape; byte-identical repeat encode; reverse-key-order digest and byte equality; declared limit order with its vacuity control; canonical key layout; domain tag reproduces the digest over the body sliced out of production's own bytes; a different tag does not; settingsDigest excluded from its own preimage WITH a positive control proving the byte surgery itself still decodes; deep-freeze of created and decoded manifests; caller detachment at depth; encoded bytes detached across calls.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the refusal surface and the sensitivity sweep, in the same test file. REFUSALS, each pinning the exact code AND the exact layer from the closed vocabulary this task publishes, with no case asserting merely that decoding failed: bytes that are not decodable JSON, or that exceed the bounded decoder's limits, pin PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_BYTES_INVALID; bytes carrying a duplicate object key pin PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DUPLICATE_KEY, which is why decodeBoundedJsonBytes must be composed rather than JSON.parse — JSON.parse keeps the LAST duplicate and destroys the provenance this code depends on; bytes that decode to a valid manifest but are not the canonical serialization (reordered object keys, added whitespace, a re-encoded number) pin PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_NONCANONICAL; and bytes whose settingsDigest does not equal the recomputed digest pin PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST_MISMATCH. Also assert that a payload the CONTRACT itself rejects (accessor, symbol key, proxy, sparse array, extra key, unsupported schema version) is refused with the contract's own code and layer preserved verbatim as the upstream, never re-coded into a codec code — the codec revalidates through parseProjectConfigurationManifest and forwards. Assert NOTHING THROWS for any hostile input. SENSITIVITY SWEEP: hand-enumerate every scalar leaf of settings — write the list out, do NOT walk the object under test, because a list derived from the subject agrees with it by construction and would keep passing after a field silently left the preimage — assert its exact positive count, and for each leaf assert that a VALID mutation changes settingsDigest while an INVALID mutation is refused with its exact code. Run and record the RED.

- DIGEST_MISMATCH / PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST / null from encode() on a digest-swapped manifest (the decode-side twin already landed in step 2 with its positive control).

UPSTREAM FORWARDING — asserts the contract's own code and layer AND `toBe` IDENTITY against the frozen contract singletons, so a codec that rebuilt a look-alike refusal fails:
- VERSION_UNSUPPORTED / PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_MANIFEST, upstream toBe PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED (schemaVersion bumped in the bytes).
- INPUT_INVALID / PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_MANIFEST, upstream toBe PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_INPUT_INVALID, for an extra key in the bytes and for five hostile OBJECT payloads: accessor, symbol key, proxy, sparse limits array, extra key.
NOTHING-THROWS: an 11-case hostile table across all three entry points (non-Uint8Array, null, proxy-over-bytes, empty, syntax, depth, array root, undefined manifest, proxy manifest, null settings, path-shaped projectId), with `expect(HOSTILE_CASES.length).toBe(11)` so a sweep that generated nothing cannot pass.

SENSITIVITY SWEEP: 53 leaves, hand-written, not walked off the fixture or the preimage. 23 named leaves written out one per line + 30 limit slots written out as explicit index literals. Counts pinned by hand three ways: NAMED_LEAVES 23, LIMIT_INDICES 30, SETTINGS_LEAVES 53, plus a distinct-label set of 53 and a cross-check that LIMIT_INDICES.length still equals PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_LIMIT_KEYS.length so a grown vocabulary cannot leave unswept slots. Each leaf gets a VALID mutation asserted to change settingsDigest and an INVALID mutation asserted to refuse with the contract code/layer/upstream.

One coupling documented in the fixture rather than hidden: orchestrationSource.objectFormat cannot be mutated alone, because SOURCE_SHA_LENGTHS binds the sha width to the format (sha1=40, sha256=64). Deep-freeze or detach every returned value; never normalize away unknown, duplicate, reordered, accessor, symbol, proxy or sparse data — invalid evidence stays typed UNKNOWN. Keep the file <=250 physical lines (`grep -c ''`); if it crosses, split canonicalization into its own module plus bridge rather than trimming the comments.

Implemented the codec plus its bridge. GREEN: `pnpm vitest run --root . packages/core/src/configuration` -> EXIT=0, 1 file / 142 tests passed. `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` -> EXIT=0.

SIZE AND BRIDGE, both measured not assumed: project-configuration-manifest.ts = 232 physical lines (`grep -c ''`), under the 250 target, so no split was needed. The bridge was written with `printf` (single LF), git added, and `git ls-files --eol packages/core/src/configuration/` reports `i/lf w/lf attr/text=auto eol=lf` — identical to every sibling. Its bytes are exactly `export * from "./project-configuration-manifest.ts";\n`, which is the literal string runtime-entrypoint.test.ts compares against.

SHAPE. Imports are the BARE "@moe/contracts" root only (four values, five types); node:crypto stays on this side of the browser boundary. Published: PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_CODEC_CODES (4 codes), PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_CODEC_LAYERS (3 layers), PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SETTINGS_DIGEST_DOMAIN, and the three functions, plus five types.

DIGEST. sha256 over tag + one NUL byte + canonical settings bytes. The preimage is built from the SETTINGS value alone, so settingsDigest is excluded structurally — there is no filter to forget. The NUL separator is unforgeable because no bounded text may contain a C0 control (isBoundedText rejects <= U+001F).

CANONICALIZATION. Recursive, no whitespace, object keys sorted, arrays left in declared order, safe integers via String(). The comment states plainly that the ARRAY rule is the load-bearing one (limits is a fixed positional table) and that the KEY SORT is currently an equivalent mutant — every record reaching the function was rebuilt by the contract parser from an already-alphabetical object literal — kept as a stated rule rather than depending on another package's source order. I would rather write that down than let a drill "discover" it later.

DECODE ORDER, deliberate and asserted: decodeBoundedJsonBytes -> duplicate-key split -> parseProjectConfigurationManifest (refusal forwarded verbatim with the contract's frozen singleton as `upstream`) -> canonical byte comparison -> digest recomputation. Parse before canonical is why an unsupported schemaVersion pins VERSION_UNSUPPORTED rather than being masked as NONCANONICAL.

ONE SNAPSHOT, and the subtle part: the snapshot is taken with `Uint8Array.prototype.slice.call(bytes)` AFTER decodeBoundedJsonBytes has returned ok, so the decoder's internal-slot brand checks (genuine Uint8Array, non-shared, non-resizable, non-detached) have already run and a Proxy or forged view never reaches the slice. The explicit prototype call is not decoration: Buffer overrides `slice` with a SHARED view, so `bytes.slice()` on a Buffer would alias caller memory instead of snapshotting it.

IMMUTABILITY. Refusals are frozen module singletons carrying nothing observed. Success results are frozen; manifests arrive already deep-frozen from the contract parser. Encoded bytes cannot be frozen (Object.freeze on a typed array with elements throws), so they are made fresh per call — detachment, not freezing, is what makes them safe, and the comment says so.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, including the reversible one DoD 5 names explicitly. For each: sha256 first, edit with the Edit tool, confirm the anchor matched once, run only the named test, reverse the edit, confirm the sha256 matches the pre-drill value — never git checkout, which reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree. D1 (DoD 5): remove ONE real production field from the canonical preimage — the named sensitivity test must go red on that leaf and only that leaf, which is what proves the sweep is bound to the production preimage rather than to its own fixture. D2: sort arrays as well as object keys in the canonicalizer — the limit-order test reddens, proving the fixed collection stays ordered. D3: drop the domain tag from the preimage — the domain-separation test reddens. D4: replace decodeBoundedJsonBytes with JSON.parse — the duplicate-key case reddens, since JSON.parse silently keeps the last duplicate and the provenance disappears. D5: accept a non-canonical byte spelling — the NONCANONICAL case reddens. D6: skip the digest recomputation on decode — the DIGEST_MISMATCH case reddens. Read every failure message and confirm it names the assertion the drill targets; a red for the wrong reason, or a drill that reddens the whole file at once, means the drill is broken rather than the guard proven.
implementationPlan.note:
Six mutation drills, all reversible, all restored. PRE-DRILL sha256 of the production file e17eefca14d7ac3c3c45bb388cc05db123a1bd7988522065f9793cffc9a898da; POST-DRILL sha256 identical; focused suite back to 142/142 green. No `git checkout` was used at any point — the harness applied and reversed by exact anchor with an ANCHOR_COUNT!=1 abort, so no drill could run against a dirty file and nothing in this shared worktree was reverted to HEAD.

D1 (the reversible one DoD 5 names) — removed policy.revision from the DIGEST preimage only, leaving the encoded bytes intact. Result: 2 failed / 140 passed. The two reds are exactly the assertions bound to the preimage: "changes the settings digest when policy.revision takes a different valid value" (the target leaf) and "derives the digest from the production domain tag over the canonical body" (which slices the full body from production's own bytes, so it notices the missing field too). The other 52 sweep leaves stayed GREEN — that selectivity is the actual evidence the sweep is bound to production and not agreeing with its own fixture.

D2 — sorted arrays as well as object keys. 4 failed / 138. The target reddened with the right message: `expected [ 'activeGoalHardEdgesMax', ...(29) ] to deeply equal [ 'providerSlotsPerProject', ...(29) ]` — the emitted table went alphabetical instead of declared. The 3 collateral reds (forged-digest, decoded-freeze, NONCANONICAL) are the round-trip tests, and they are red for the correct reason: a sorted limit table is no longer a valid positional table, which is precisely the guarantee sorting destroys. Read and accounted for, not waved past.

D3 — dropped the domain tag from the preimage. 1 failed / 141: only "derives the digest from the production domain tag over the canonical body". Cleanest possible signal that domain separation is a property here rather than a comment.

D4 — replaced decodeBoundedJsonBytes with JSON.parse over the decoded text. 2 failed / 140. Target red: "pins DUPLICATE_KEY, which JSON.parse would have silently swallowed". Second red is informative rather than collateral noise — "pins BYTES_INVALID at the codec layer for undecodable bytes" also fell, because JSON.parse happily accepts the 70-deep array that MAX_JSON_DEPTH refuses. So the drill proves composition on BOTH legs the bounded decoder is here for: duplicate-key provenance AND the input bounds.

D5 — neutralised the canonical byte comparison. 1 failed / 141: only "pins NONCANONICAL for reordered keys, added whitespace and a respelled number".

D6 — removed the digest recomputation from decode. 1 failed / 141: only "excludes settingsDigest from its own preimage yet refuses a forged one".

Every red was read, not counted. No drill reddened the file wholesale, and no drill reddened on an assertion other than the one it targets.

NOT DRILLED, AND I AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN LETTING IT LOOK COVERED: removing the object-key `.sort()` kills nothing. Gated, reviewed, committed as 268b2ce (6 files, 891 insertions).

A REAL DEFECT FOUND BY THE ADVERSARIAL PASS, FIXED WITH A REGRESSION TEST. Decode snapshotted the caller's bytes with `Uint8Array.prototype.slice.call(bytes)`. That call consults `Symbol.species`, so a genuine Uint8Array SUBCLASS — which passes every one of the bounded decoder's internal-slot brand checks — could run caller code inside a function whose whole contract is that it only ever refuses. Two consequences: a throwing species getter throws straight out of decode (violating DoD 3's "no malformed input throws"), and a species returning a longer buffer would have the canonical comparison read bytes other than the ones actually decoded. Proven before fixing: the new test failed with `Error: species trap` raised at project-configuration-manifest.ts:224. The snapshot now uses `new Uint8Array(bytes)`, which copies from internal slots and calls nothing the caller controls. The test arms a throwing species, asserts via a CONTROL that `Uint8Array.prototype.slice.call(trapped)` really does throw, then requires decode to succeed and return the matching digest — so the guard cannot rot back without going red. 142 -> 143 tests.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED: reusing the contracts package's canonicalization (canonicalUnsignedManifestBytes / canonicalJson / isCanonicalText). They exist in packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.ts but are deliberately NOT on the package root — a prior QA pass proved that with an explicit negative control — and task rail 1 forbids deep-importing contract internals. @moe/core therefore writes its own canonical-bytes function. That is the only legal path, not an oversight, and the production comment should say so; the alternative (publishing them from contracts) is out of scope and belongs to the now-DONE task-0c21ba2f. REJECTED: JSON.parse in decode. DoD 3 requires composing decodeBoundedJsonBytes specifically, and the reason is duplicate-key provenance: JSON.parse keeps the LAST duplicate silently, which destroys the very evidence PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DUPLICATE_KEY exists to report. Drill D4 pins it. REJECTED: filtering settingsDigest out of the preimage. It lives on the MANIFEST and never on settings, so hashing the settings value excludes it structurally — no filter to forget, no filter to drift. The test still asserts both halves, because a codec that ignored the field entirely would pass the naive version of that assertion. REJECTED: sorting arrays during canonicalization. Object key order must be irrelevant, but `limits` is a FIXED ORDERED table whose order is part of the contract; sorting it would make a reordered table hash identically and silently retire the ordering guarantee. Both directions are asserted and D2 drills it. REJECTED: deriving the sensitivity leaf list by walking the settings object — a list derived from the subject agrees with it by construction and keeps passing after a field quietly leaves the preimage, which is exactly the defect DoD 5's reversible mutation is designed to catch.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE 69-COUNT PIN AND THE LINE-COUNT RAIL PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. One demands new rows in the surface test, the other forbids index.ts from growing. Both are satisfiable — the surface test has no line budget, and index.ts has same-specifier blocks that reflow — but discovering either during the final gate reads as an unrelated break. Handle both in step 5, deliberately.
2. A SORTED LIMIT TABLE SILENTLY RETIRES THE ORDER GUARANTEE. Object keys must sort; arrays must not. Assert both directions or the canonicalizer is half-tested.
3. DOMAIN SEPARATION IS UNTESTABLE BY INSPECTION. Without the same-body-different-tag assertion, 'domain-separated' is a comment. It must be a test.
4. JSON.parse WOULD PASS ALMOST EVERY TEST while destroying duplicate-key provenance — the one code it silently makes unreachable is PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DUPLICATE_KEY.
5. A SENSITIVITY SWEEP DERIVED FROM THE SUBJECT IS VACUOUS. Hand-write the leaf list and its count; DoD 5's reversible field removal is the check that the list is bound to production.
6. TYPE-ONLY PUBLICATION LOOKS COMPLETE AND IMPORTS AS NOTHING. `export type` is erased at runtime; the surface test must reach real runtime values.
7. THE BRIDGE IS LOAD-BEARING AND EASY TO BOTCH. Intra-package imports use `.js` specifiers, so a missing bridge breaks runtime loading while tsc stays green, and a CRLF bridge on Windows differs from every sibling. Verify with `git ls-files --eol`.
8. SHARED WORKTREE. .moe/**, apps/**, adapters/** and packages/store/** carry other agents' uncommitted work. Never git add -A, never stash, never reset; git add the three new files explicitly before committing by pathspec.
